chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

A man who stole from the war booty items for which cutting (of the hand) is obligatory. He said: It is looked at to see how much he takes. If what he took is less than his share, he is flogged and his full property is returned to him. And if he took equal to what is his, there is nothing upon him. And if he took an excess equal to the value of a 'mijan' (a small leather bag or pouch), which is a quarter of a dinar, he is cut.

key_terms.مِجَنٍّ: A small leather bag or pouch (unit of measure/value)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for stealing from war booty in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the hadd of amputation for stealing from war booty (maghnam) is not automatic but contingent on the thief exceeding their entitled share by a specific threshold—defined here as the value of a shield (mijan), equivalent to a quarter of a dinar. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between simple misappropriation of one's own portion and the distinct crime of theft from the communal treasury, emphasizing proportionality in penal justice. The hadith reflects the practical application of fiqh in military contexts, ensuring that soldiers are not penalized for taking their due while maintaining strict accountability for excess.
